resources.purpose: Account identity, consent, credentials, notification choices and per-user synchronization state.
resources.retention: For the account lifetime; credentials are replaced on reconnect and deleted with the account.
resources.erasure: Explicit account deletion cascades through user-owned rows. Terms evidence is deleted with the account.

resources.purpose: Display listening history, rankings and changes over time.
resources.retention: Until the user deletes the corresponding data or account; inactivity alone never authorizes deletion.
resources.erasure: Delete-data controls and account deletion remove the user's rows by cascading foreign keys.

resources.purpose: Shared Spotify metadata needed to render user history, statistics and leagues without duplicating catalog rows.
resources.retention: Referenced rows remain; unreferenced tracks, albums and artists are removed after 90 days. Unreferenced genres are removed nightly.
resources.erasure: Nightly cleanup deletes only rows with no history, snapshot, ranking or league reference.

resources.purpose: Publish a playlist snapshot to an intended recipient and track safe refresh/download/revocation state.
resources.retention: Active claimed shares remain until revoked or an account is deleted; unclaimed shares expire after 7 days; revoked payloads expire after 30 days.
resources.erasure: Revocation removes recipient access immediately and scheduled cleanup removes expired payloads and tombstones.

resources.purpose: Consent-based stats access, invitations, notification delivery, blocks and abuse review.
resources.retention: Approved access and blocks remain until revoked/unblocked; expired invitations and declined/revoked requests expire after 30 days; reviewed reports after 180 days; pending reports remain for review.
resources.erasure: Participant actions remove access; nightly cleanup removes policy-expired state; account deletion cascades participant records.

resources.purpose: Operate leagues, rounds, recommendations, scoring, playlists, invitations and optional notifications.
resources.retention: League history remains until owner deletion so past scores and recommendations remain available. Expired invite/rejoin state is removed after a 30-day grace period; delivery logs follow the operational log policy.
resources.erasure: League deletion cascades league content; leaving removes membership access but preserves score integrity; account deletion applies database cascades.

resources.purpose: Temporarily compare or merge selected playlists and exchange room proposals/messages.
resources.retention: Uploads are short-lived; expired or revoked rooms and participant content are removed after 30 days.
resources.erasure: Room revocation blocks access immediately; existing room cleanup removes the room graph after its grace period.

resources.purpose: Configuration, administration, deployment state, job execution, health, audit and aggregate cleanup monitoring.
resources.retention: Configuration remains until replaced. Successful/cancelled job logs are 30 days, failures and resolved alerts are 90 days, credential audit is 90 days, successful retention summaries are 90 days.
resources.erasure: Scheduled operational and retention jobs redact error details and delete expired logs; records contain identifiers only where needed for incident diagnosis.

resources.purpose: Rate limiting, bounded chunk uploads and short synchronization leases.
resources.retention: Rate limits 2 days, uploads and upload tracks 1 hour, expired leases 1 day.
resources.erasure: Automated cleanup deletes expired rows; no user-facing history depends on them.

resources.purpose: Session continuity, offline application assets and explicitly enabled local Spotify data.
resources.retention: As defined in config/browser-storage-inventory.json; session-only state ends with the tab and persistent state remains until logout/delete-data/browser removal.
resources.erasure: The application's logout and delete-data actions clear scoped browser records; users can also clear site data.

resources.purpose: Encrypted disaster recovery after infrastructure failure.
resources.retention: Maximum 30-day rolling retention; no backup is used as an application archive.
resources.erasure: Live data is inaccessible immediately after deletion and ages out of encrypted backups within 30 days. A disaster restore must reapply deletion records before normal access resumes.
